title: Generalized Weakness
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a child who presents with generalized weakness, oliguria, cola-colored (dark brown) urine, periorbital and ankle edema (2+ pitting), and hypertension 1-4 weeks after a streptococcal pharyngitis or skin infection (impetigo). This is acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis — an immune complex-mediated (type III hypersensitivity) disease. Antigen-antibody complexes deposit in the glomerular basement membrane → complement activation → glomerular inflammation. Labs: UA shows hematuria (dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts — pathognomonic), proteinuria (<3.5g/day — nephritic, not nephrotic range). Low C3 complement (returns to normal in 6-8 weeks). Elevated ASO titer (pharyngitis) or anti-DNase B (skin infection). BMP shows elevated BUN/Cr (acute kidney injury). Diagnosis is clinical. Renal biopsy only if rapidly progressive GN or atypical course. Treatment: supportive — salt/fluid restriction, diuretics (furosemide) for hypertension and edema, antihypertensives if needed. Prognosis excellent in children (>95% complete recovery). Antibiotics if active strep infection. No immunosuppression needed.
chief_complaint: Generalized weakness, cola-colored urine, periorbital/ankle edema

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Assess for edema, respiratory distress from fluid overload.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Recent strep infection — assess for pneumonia signs.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities
stacks.finding: 2+ pitting edema around ankles — classic nephritic finding.

stacks.label: Urinalysis with microscopy
stacks.finding: Dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts (pathognomonic), proteinuria (nephritic range <3.5g/day). Cola-colored urine from hematuria.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP
stacks.finding: Elevated BUN/Cr — acute kidney injury. Hyperkalemia possible.

stacks.label: C3, C4 complement
stacks.finding: Low C3 (returns to normal in 6-8 weeks). C4 normal — distinguishes PSGN from other GN.

stacks.label: ASO titer / Anti-DNase B
stacks.finding: ASO elevated after strep pharyngitis. Anti-DNase B after skin infection.

stacks.label: Renal ultrasound
stacks.finding: Normal or slightly enlarged kidneys. Rule out obstruction.

stacks.label: Furosemide (Lasix)
stacks.finding: Loop diuretic for edema and hypertension management.

stacks.label: Antibiotics (Penicillin) if active strep
stacks.finding: Treat active streptococcal infection. Does not alter course of GN but prevents spread.

physical_exam.respiratory: Assess for pulmonary edema from fluid overload.

decoys.label: Immunosuppression (steroids / cyclophosphamide)
decoys.reason_wrong: PSGN is self-limited, immune complex-mediated. Immunosuppression is NOT indicated. Supportive care only — spontaneous recovery in 95%+ of children.

teach_me_steps.order: Nephritic syndrome: hematuria + HTN + edema + AKI
teach_me_steps.reasoning: RBC casts = pathognomonic for glomerulonephritis. Low C3 (normal C4). Elevated ASO/anti-DNase B. 1-4 weeks after strep infection. Type III hypersensitivity.
Self-limited disease. Salt/fluid restriction + furosemide + BP control. Antibiotics if active strep (doesn't alter GN course). >95% children recover completely.

case_summary: PSGN in child. Cola urine + periorbital/ankle edema + HTN + AKI 1-4 weeks after strep pharyngitis. UA: RBC casts + proteinuria. Low C3. Supportive care: fluid restriction + furosemide. Excellent prognosis.
